messages.text: Hi Sarah, my browser is not finding 192.168.4.1

That address only loads while your phone or laptop is connected to the miner's own setup Wi-Fi. Join that network, turn off mobile data, and type http://192.168.4.1 (http, not https). If it was already set up, it's on your home Wi-Fi now under a different address, which your router's device list will show.

Is the Thor P2 already in your hands?
Yes. Sorry for the delay, but I've got it connected to wifi now

Nice work. Your router's connected-devices list will show the Thor's new address. Type it into your browser the same way, with http://. That opens the dashboard, where you add a pool and the Bitcoin address your sats get paid to.

Do you already have a wallet address ready, or do you want help picking a pool?
I am not finding it as a connected device

Most small miners like this only join 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi. If your router combines 2.4 and 5 GHz under one name, or the password had a typo, it won't connect. One quick check: if the miner's setup network shows up again in your Wi-Fi list, it didn't join, so redo the setup and retype the password carefully.

Does the Thor's setup network still show up on your phone?
My fiber optic 'router' probably does combine into 1 name

That's probably it. The router's admin address and login are usually printed on a sticker on the box itself. Log in, find the Wi-Fi settings, and either turn off "band steering" (sometimes called "Smart Connect") or set up a separate 2.4 GHz network. A guest network on 2.4 GHz works too.

Then rejoin the Thor's setup Wi-Fi, go back to http://192.168.4.1, and choose the new 2.4 GHz network.

Want to tell me the router's brand so I can point you to the right setting?
ZYCEL AX6000 Model# EX5512-TO or T0

That's a Zyxel, and they usually make this easy. Go to http://192.168.1.1 and log in with the admin password printed on the router's sticker. Under Network Setting > Wireless, uncheck "Keep 2.4G and 5G wireless network name the same" and give the 2.4 GHz network its own name, like "Home-2G". Your internet provider's version may name things a little differently.

Then go back to the Thor's setup page and choose Home-2G. Did it find the setting?
I was able to connect the P2 via ethernet but I am not able to connect to any 192.168 addresses

Let's find your network's real address first. Your router may not use 192.168.1.x at all, and a VPN or mobile data will also block these local pages.

On the device you're browsing with, check that it's on your home Wi-Fi with any VPN off. Then find the "Router" or "Default Gateway" address. On Windows, type ipconfig in Command Prompt. On an iPhone, tap the (i) next to your Wi-Fi network.

What address does it show?
Are you looking for LAN IP Subnet #s?

Close. "LAN IP" is the router's own address, so if you're looking at that screen, you're already logged into the router. Now find the DHCP client list or connected devices page on that same router screen. The T. should show up there, connected by ethernet, with an address next to it. Type that address into your browser with http:// in front.

What's the LAN IP it shows?

That explains it. Your network uses 192.168.40.x, not 192.168.1.x, so the router is almost certainly at http://192.168.40.1. Open that address and log in with the admin password from the sticker. Then go to the connected devices or DHCP client list. The T. should show up there as a wired device, with an address like 192.168.40.something.

Do you see it in that list?

MY APOLOGIES...the router in my room is an extender...the info on the back of the says 192.168.1.1  In the Plume app that Point Broadband fiber network connects to, the LAN IP Subnet shows as 192.168.40.x

No need to apologize, that helps. Plume networks are run from the app, not a browser page, which is why 192.168.1.1 goes nowhere.

In the Plume app, open the list of devices. Look for a new wired device. It might show up as "Espressif" or with an unknown name. Tap it to see its IP address, which will look like 192.168.40.something. Type that into your browser with http:// in front, using a device on the same Wi-Fi.

Do you see a new device in the list?
I did see expressif...hold while I find it again...thank you

Take your time. That's almost certainly the Thor, since Espressif makes the chip inside it. When you tap it, you'll see an address like 192.168.40.something. Open that in your browser and you'll be on the Thor's dashboard, ready to add your pool and wallet address. I'm right here.
Shows Offline and last online on 10/22/26

That one's an older entry from October 22, not the Thor today. It may be another device, or an earlier setup attempt.

Unplug the Thor's power, check the ethernet cable is clicked in at both ends, then power it back on. Give it a couple of minutes and refresh the Plume device list. Look for a new device that shows Online.

Do the lights on the Thor's ethernet port blink when it's plugged in?
Yes, I do see Espressif on my phone

Good. Where do you see it? If Espressif is on the Plume device list and marked Online, tap it to get the 192.168.40.something address and open that.

If it's on your phone's Wi-Fi list as a network, the Thor is in setup mode. Join that network, turn off mobile data, and go to http://192.168.4.1. Then carefully re-enter your home Wi-Fi name and password.

Which of the two is it?
FYI, the Thor address is 192.168.40.142

That's the one. On your phone or laptop, on home Wi-Fi with mobile data and any VPN off, open http://192.168.40.142. That's the Thor's dashboard. In its settings you add a pool address and your Bitcoin wallet address, save, and it starts hashing.

Do you want to go for the solo block shot, or steady small payouts from a pool?
OMG, I finally got it!  Thank you! Let's start with solo

Congrats, it's running! For solo, you can use either of these pools in the Thor's pool settings:

Public Pool: URL public-pool.io, port 21496
CKPool Solo: URL solo.ckpool.org, port 3333

For the username, enter your Bitcoin wallet address. Optionally add a worker name after it, like yourAddress.thor. For the password, enter x. Save, and it restarts.

Every ten minutes or so, it now takes a shot at a full 3.125 BTC block, paid straight to your own wallet if it hits.

Do you have a Bitcoin wallet address ready?
I believe I got one for a Luqee miner through Coinbase.  What do you recommend?

The C. address will work, as long as it's a Bitcoin (BTC) address. Those start with bc1, 1 or 3.

For solo, though, I'd use a wallet you hold the keys to, like BlueWallet or Sparrow, or a hardware wallet if you have one. If you hit a block, the 3.125 BTC lands in a wallet only you control. Exchanges can also rotate deposit addresses, and that's not something you want to find out after the fact.

Want help setting one up?
May I pause this for now and come back after lunch? I want to make sure that I get this right.

Of course, enjoy your lunch. Here's everything you need for when you're back:

Thor dashboard: http://192.168.40.142
Solo pool: public-pool.io, port 21496 (or solo.ckpool.org, port 3333)
Username: your BTC wallet address
Password: x

The hard part's done, it's on your network. When you're back, just tell me which wallet you went with and we'll finish the setup.
Fyi, I rebooted the Thor and the address is now 192.168.40.40  Thank you again and see you after lunch

Got it, the dashboard is now http://192.168.40.40. The router hands out a new address each time it restarts. To keep it fixed, look for an IP reservation option on the Espressif device in the Plume app, then you won't have to hunt for it again.

Enjoy lunch, and see you after.
Ok, first...are you AI?

Yes, I'm the store's AI shopping assistant. The HeliumDeploy team is online right now, so if you'd rather finish with a person, just say so and I'll bring them in.

Otherwise, let's finish your solo setup. Did you pick a wallet over lunch, or are you sticking with Coinbase?
No, I'm good...I just didn't want to keep a human waiting while I intermittently interact here.  I'm going to research BlueWallet and Sparrow as you recommended and will return once I make my choice.
Used the chat-interview skill

Sounds good. One tip for your research: BlueWallet is the easy phone option, and Sparrow is a desktop app that gives you more control. Either way, write your recovery words on paper and keep them offline.

Your Thor's dashboard is at http://192.168.40.40 when you're ready. I'll be here.
